Article Title: 'At no cost' will Mann complete tenure: Congress' Warring predicts AAP govt collapse in Punjab
Article Text:
Congress Warring predicts AAP govt collapse in Punjab (PTI photo)

NEW DELHI: Punjab Congress president Amarinder Singh Raja Warring took a dig at chief minister Bhagwant Mann , saying the ongoing Vidhan Sabha session could be his last. The sharp jibe at Punjab CM came months prior to Punjab's assembly elections set for early next year.Warring also claimed that the Aam Aadmi Party government could soon lose its majority because of growing discontent among its MLAs.While bidding farewell to Mann, Warring said the chief minister would "at no cost" complete his tenure. He claimed that even if the Punjab assembly elections are held as scheduled in February 2027, Mann would not remain chief minister until then."The Aam Aadmi Party is likely to implode very soon as the government is losing its majority. Many MLAs are just waiting for the opportune moment, which is not very far," he said.Warring claimed that most AAP MLAs were "completely alienated and disillusioned" with their own government. "For four and a half years, they have felt suffocated and they are now waiting for the breather," he said.The Punjab Congress chief alleged that despite receiving a strong mandate, the AAP government had failed both the people of Punjab and its own MLAs."Mann has proved to be the worst ever chief minister Punjab had, for which they will never forgive him," he said.Warring also criticised CM Mann for continuing to rely on his image as a comedian after becoming chief minister.He said Mann had failed to understand that his role had changed after taking charge of the state."Unfortunately, Mann could not make the difference that his stage had changed and he was no longer required to survive through narrating jokes and anecdotes. People of Punjab had not elected you to make them laugh, for that they already had enough of your comedy," he said.The PCC president said people had voted for Mann expecting "badlaav" (change), but alleged that he had instead given up his authority to "outsiders" to protect his position as chief minister."Instead, you surrendered all your authority to outsiders while guarding your chief ministerial chair, for which you sacrificed the interests of Punjab. History will never forgive you for that," Warring warned CM Mann.Earlier, on August 5, Warring said he wanted to contest the 2027 assembly election against Mann and urged the Congress leadership to field him from Mann's constituency.Addressing a gathering in Faridkot, Warring said the final decision would be taken by Congress leaders Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi."While Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge have to make a decision. I am not in a position to do that. Either don't field me at all, or if you do field me, field me against Bhagwant Mann. I will contest," he said.The remarks come as political parties prepare for the 2027 Punjab assembly elections. The AAP, Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) have already started preparations for the polls.The AAP won the 2022 Punjab assembly elections with a strong majority, forming its first government in the state and ending the Congress' tenure in power.
Article Summary: Punjab congress president amarinder singh raja warring took a dig at chief minister bhagwant mann. The sharp jibe at punjab cm came months prior to punjab's assembly elections set for early next year. Warring also claimed that the aam aadmi party government could soon lose its majority.

Article Title: Jharkhand protest: Police defend ‘mild force’, to scan CCTV for miscreants - key points
Article Text:
The students have been protesting against alleged irregularities in JPSC and JSSC recruitment examinations.

Police to analyse CCTV footage

DC says stone was thrown at jawan

NEW DELHI: Police will examine CCTV footage to identify people they allege disrupted a largely peaceful student protest in Ranchi on Monday, as top officials defended the use of “mild” and “minimum” force to disperse job aspirants marching towards the Jharkhand Assembly.The agitation, which entered its 17th day, saw police use water cannons, tear gas and lathicharge during the ‘Vidhan Sabha Gherao’ march by students protesting alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations conducted by the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) and Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC).While police said protesters refused repeated requests to clear the route and alleged that some people damaged barricades, pelted stones and tried to stop vehicles, student protesters accused police of using force without warning. An injured protester claimed that at least 100 young men were beaten during the lathicharge.Ranchi SSP Rakesh Ranjan said police would examine CCTV footage from the protest to identify those allegedly responsible for disrupting the demonstration."Police will analyse CCTV footage to identify anti-social elements who disrupted the peaceful students' protest," Rakesh Ranjan told reporters.Ranjan said 14 police personnel were injured during Monday’s protest, including one who suffered a major injury. According to him, police used only the minimum force required to bring the situation under control."We had previously communicated--and it was agreed--that the siege of the Legislative Assembly complex would be entirely peaceful. The police exercised considerable restraint, and we allowed the students to proceed gradually as far as they wished to go. We employed the minimum amount of force necessary based on the unfolding situation, and as a result, the current situation is peaceful," SSP Ranjan said in the joint presser.He alleged that some protesters repeatedly tried to create a disturbance, including attempts to stop vehicles and objects being thrown at them."The police used minimal force; we allowed the protesters to do whatever they wished to do all day long. We made every effort to reason with them and persuade them gently. There were some individuals who did not listen and repeatedly tried to create a ruckus. Attempts were made to stop passing vehicles--including those of officials--and objects like shoes and slippers were hurled at them," Ranchi SSP added.Ranchi Deputy Commissioner Manjunath Bhajantri also defended the police action, saying the force had exercised restraint throughout the protest and intervened only after a police personnel was allegedly put in danger."On July 24, some students and student leaders launched an indefinite protest. Since it had started without permission--and given the upcoming Durand Cup and Tribal Festival--a request was made for them to relocate; they subsequently moved to Jaipal Singh Stadium on July 28," DC Bhajantri said.He said the protest continued at the stadium while talks were held between student representatives and a state government committee. The agitation later intensified after student organisations called for a siege of the Assembly."Throughout this, our police force demonstrated restraint and strove to avoid using force. Amidst this, certain anti-social elements attempted to provoke the police and officials; a stone was thrown at a jawan, and another jawan was being crushed by the crowd, placing his life in danger. Consequently, the police used mild force to rescue the jawan," the DC said.Bhajantri said protesters had also refused repeated appeals by police and magistrates to clear a route towards the Assembly."Despite repeated requests from the police and magistrates to clear a path, the protesters refused to do so; therefore, mild force was used to remove them and normalise the situation," he said.The DC also called for those allegedly attempting to disturb the peace to be identified."I urge that the anti-social elements who are joining in to incite such situations be identified. The police will also take further action to identify them," he said.
Article Summary: Ranchi ssp rakesh ranjan says police will examine cctv footage from the protest to identify those allegedly responsible for disrupting the demonstration. The agitation, which entered its 17th day, saw police use water cannons, tear gas and lathicharge. The students have been protesting against alleged irregularities in jpsc and jssc recruitment examinations.

Article Title: Number of govt elementary schools down 10,000 in a year
Article Text:
Data showed the number of elementary-level govt schools declined from 8,89,806 in 2024-25 to 8,79,940 in 2025-26

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The number of govt elementary schools across the country fell by nearly 10,000 in a year, with Meghalaya, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh recording the steepest declines, according to data tabled in the Lok Sabha on Monday.UDISE+ data showed that the number of elementary-level govt schools declined from 8,89,806 in 2024-25 to 8,79,940 in 2025-26 - a reduction of 9,866 schools, or about 1.1%.The govt data was provided in response to a question from DMK MP T R Baalu on whether a large number of elementary schools had been closed because of insufficient student strength and the steps being taken to prevent dropouts. However, the education ministry did not specify how many of the schools were actually closed due to lack of students, while furnishing the overall number of govt elementary schools in the two academic years.Meghalaya recorded the biggest numerical decline, with the number of govt elementary schools falling from 7,633 to 5,459, a drop of 2,174. Telangana followed with a reduction of 1,961 schools, from 22,983 to 21,022, while Andhra Pradesh saw its count decline by 1,446, from 37,449 to 36,003.Madhya Pradesh had 1,043 fewer schools, Karnataka 615, West Bengal 587, Rajasthan 473 and Maharashtra 357. Himachal Pradesh recorded a decline of 259 schools, while Assam had 209 fewer.Uttar Pradesh, which continues to have the largest network of govt elementary schools, saw the number fall marginally from 1,34,115 to 1,33,948.Not every state recorded a decline. Bihar's count rose from 66,803 to 66,915, while Chhattisgarh increased from 43,836 to 43,853. The numbers remained unchanged in Jammu & Kashmir, Puducherry and the Andaman & Nicobar Islands.The ministry said opening, closing and rationalisation of schools fall within the jurisdiction of state and UT govts since education is on the Concurrent List.At the same time, it said access to schooling had improved. The Gross Access Ratio rose between 2018-19 and 2025-26 from 96.49 to 98.14 at upper-primary level, from 88.24 to 95.05 at secondary level and from 65.05 to 94.79 at higher-secondary level.The Centre said states were being supported through Samagra Shiksha and PM POSHAN, besides assistance for school infrastructure, residential schools and hostels, transport facilities, enrolment drives, textbooks and uniforms to curb dropouts and improve enrolment.
Article Summary: Data showed the number of elementary-level govt schools declined from 8,89,806 in 2024-25 to 8,79,940 in 2025-26. Meghalaya, telangana and andhra pradesh recorded the steepest declines, according to data tabled in the lok sabha on monday.

Article Title: 'Our mother tongue is as pure as our mother': Vijay moves Tamil anthem resolution; DMK, AIADMK back it
Article Text:
Tamil Thai Vazhthu is an invocation to Mother Tamil from Manonmaniam, a play written by Manonmaniam Sundaranar in 1891. (Photo: PTI)

What does the resolution say?

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday moved a government resolution in the assembly making the rendition of Tamil Thai Vazhthu, the state song, mandatory at the beginning of official programmes across the state.Moving the resolution in the state assembly, Vijay said his Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam government would not compromise on Tamil Nadu's linguistic and cultural rights and urged legislators to set aside political differences in supporting the measure."Our mother tongue is as pure as our mother," Vijay said in an emotive speech, adding that, "Tamil is not only a language but also our life and emotions.""Tamil means pride, Tamil means power. The moment you say 'Tamil', the entire Tamil Nadu will come together and stand as one," he said."Tamil Thai Vazhthu must hold the first place in Tamil Nadu. Giving first place to Tamil Thaai Vaazhthu is our state right," he noted."Saying that Tamil Thai Vazhthu should be sung first does not need to become a political debate," the Tamil nadu CM said, appealing to members across party lines to support the resolution.Under the resolution, Tamil Thai Vazhthu will be sung first at programmes held by educational institutions, universities, government offices, public sector undertakings and other public institutions in Tamil Nadu.The resolution received support from both DMK and AIADMK legislators, with members backing the government's move to mandate the singing of the state song at official functions.The move comes amid a recent advisory from the Union home ministry asking states and Union territories to comply with its January 28 directive on playing Vande Mataram before the National Anthem at official events.It also comes against the backdrop of a July 9 communication from the ministry of home affairs regarding the singing of state songs at official programmes.The resolution describes Tamil Thai Vazhthu as an expression of respect for the Tamil language and culture and links its mandatory rendition to the linguistic and cultural rights guaranteed under the Constitution."Therefore, this House ( Tamil Nadu Assembly ) emphasises that "Tamil Thai Vazhthu" is an expression of respect for the Tamil language and Tamil culture. In accordance with the linguistic and cultural rights guaranteed by the Constitution of India, and with a view to preserving the Cultural identity of Tamil Nadu, the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly unanimously resolves that "Tamil Thai Vazhthu" shall be mandatorily sung first, before the commencement of programmes held by all Educational Institutions, Universities, Government Offices, Public Sector Undertakings and other Public Institutions in Tamil Nadu," the resolution said.The resolution also notes that Tamil is one of the world's oldest classical languages and describes Tamil civilisation as one of the world's oldest cultural traditions.Tamil Nadu had first directed that Tamil Thai Vazhthu be sung at the beginning of official functions through a government order issued on November 23, 1970.The state government formally accorded the song the status of the state song on December 12, 2021, making its rendition mandatory at official programmes and institutions across the state.Tamil Thai Vazhthu is an invocation to Mother Tamil from Manonmaniam, a play written by Manonmaniam Sundaranar in 1891.
Article Summary: Tamil nadu chief minister c joseph vijay on monday moved a government resolution in the assembly making the rendition of tamil thai vazhthu, the state song, mandatory at the beginning of official programmes across the state. Vijay said his tamilaga vettri kazhagam government would not compromise on tamil nadu's linguistic and cultural rights.

Article Title: Government may be going slow on FCRA to woo DMK, NCP(SP) for delimitation
Article Text:
The Bill was introduced in Lok Sabha on March 25 but has not been taken up for discussion yet, amid fierce protest from opposition parties and minority groups, especially Christian bodies

Government may prefer full-fledged debate on FCRA to address criticism against the bill

NEW DELHI: The passage of FCRA amendment bill is not in Lok Sabha's agenda for Monday as Parliament's monsoon session enters its last week, giving rise to the view that government may be going slow on the contentious piece of legislation to sweeten the deal for parties such as DMK and NCP(SP), which are opposed to its provisions and are being seen by the governing alliance as prospective backers for its delimitation exercise.Sources said the meeting of LS's business advisory committee, where upcoming agenda items are finalised, on Monday will give more clarity as a schedule for discussion on the bill should be fixed if it has to be taken up for passage in the remaining four days of Parliament's monsoon session ending on Aug 13. Monday's agenda includes the introduction of four bills but makes no mention of the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill.The Bill was introduced in Lok Sabha on March 25 but has not been taken up for discussion yet, amid fierce protest from opposition parties and minority groups, especially Christian bodies.Christian groups, which are a major recipient of foreign funding, have decried the proposed amendments, saying it threatens their charitable works and will allow the government to seize their assets if their FCRA licence is withdrawn or not renewed.What has, though, made things politically trickier for the BJP is the support extended by DMK president M K Stalin to the demand of a delegation representing churches of different denominations in their meeting with home minister Amit Shah that the bill be either withdrawn or sent to a joint parliamentary committee for scrutiny.With the government looking to assuage DMK’s concerns to get it on board before it makes a fresh bid for Parliament’s nod for its delimitation exercise, coupled with implementation of the women’s reservation law from 2029, it may not like to put the regional party on the defensive by bringing up the FCRA bill, some MPs said.Supriya Sule of NCP SP, another party being eyed by the government as a probable supporter for the amendment bill, has also opposed the FCRA bill.Mizoram CM Lalduhoma had told the media after joining a group of Church bodies from his state for a meeting with Amit Shah on Thursday that he was told that a debate on the bill is expected to be held on Aug 12.The continuing impasse in Parliament due to the opposition’s protests has added uncertainty as the government will prefer a full-fledged debate so that the home ministry could address the criticism around the bill.
Article Summary: Government may prefer full-fledged debate on fcra to address criticism against the bill. Bill was introduced in lok sabha on march 25 but has not been taken up for discussion yet. Christian groups, which are a major recipient of foreign funding, have decried the proposed amendments.

Article Title: Sharad Pawar’s MPs to meet PM Modi; Congress asks them to delink women’s quota, delimitation
Article Text:
NCP(SP) to meet PM Modi, delegation to raise issues affecting Maharashtra,.

NCP (SP) MPs to raise Maharashtra issues

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A delegation of eight MPs from Sharad Pawar-led NCP (SP) is scheduled to meet Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday during the ongoing Monsoon Session of Parliament.Ahead of the meeting, the Congress has urged its alliance partner to convey the INDIA bloc's opposition to linking the implementation of women's reservation with the proposed delimitation exercise.AICC secretary Sachin Sawant urged the NCP (SP) delegation to press Modi for the immediate implementation of the Women's Reservation Act, passed in 2023, without waiting for delimitation."It is learnt that the MPs of the Nationalist Congress Party - Sharadchandra Pawar will be meeting Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday regarding issues concerning Maharashtra. We urge them to firmly convey to Prime Minister Modi that the INDIA Alliance's unequivocal position is that the Women's Reservation Act, passed in 2023, must be implemented immediately and should not be linked to delimitation," Sawant posted on X on Sunday."It is important that the unity of the INDIA Alliance and its opposition to the Modi government on this issue is made unequivocally clear," he added.The Congress' appeal comes ahead of the meeting between PM Modi and eight NCP (SP) MPs, led by party MP Supriya Sule.Sule had said on Saturday that the delegation would raise issues affecting Maharashtra, including farmer suicides, the water crisis and problems caused by rapid urbanisation."We - some MPs and I - were talking about that Prime Minister must be apprised about the problems in Maharashtra. There is water related issues, farmer suicides, and problems being faced due to urbanisation," Sule said at a press conference in Mumbai.BJP leader Navneet Rana welcomed the proposed meeting, saying elected representatives should be able to raise issues concerning Maharashtra's development with the Prime Minister."I feel that if MPs from Sharad Pawar 's party are meeting PM Modi for the sake of Maharashtra's development--driven by the belief that the state needs to progress further--then such a meeting is certainly not a bad thing," Rana said."While all sorts of speculations are being made, I believe any such speculation ultimately bodes well for Maharashtra; there could be nothing better than them approaching the PM to advocate for the state's development," she added.The dispute centres on the government's proposed delimitation exercise and its connection with the implementation of the women's reservation law. The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026, introduced in the Lok Sabha on April 16, proposed increasing the strength of the House to 850 seats and sought to expedite the implementation of the Women's Reservation Act passed in 2023.The bill, however, failed to secure the constitutionally required two-thirds majority of members present and voting and was not passed during the extended Budget Session.The Congress and other opposition parties have backed women's reservation but oppose making its implementation dependent on delimitation. They have argued that the reservation provisions should be implemented immediately rather than waiting for the expansion and redrawing of Lok Sabha constituencies.
Article Summary: Ncp(sp) to meet pm modi, delegation to raise issues affecting maharashtra. Ncp (sp) mps to raise maharashtra issues. Congress has urged its alliance partner to convey the india bloc's opposition to linking the implementation of women's reservation with the proposed delimitation exercise.

Article Title: Jharkhand assembly gherao: Security stepped up with 750m curbs, barbed-wire barricades
Article Text:
Jharkhand Police imposed prohibitory orders around the Assembly and strengthened security across the city as students marched against alleged recruitment exam irregularities.

March to begin at 10:30 am

Security stepped up across Ranchi

Schools to remain closed

BJP alleges Aditya Sahu placed under house arrest

Students allege police stopping protesters from reaching Ranchi

Students asked to maintain peace

NEW DELHI: Ranchi is under heightened security on Monday as protesting students prepare to march to the Jharkhand Vidhan Sabha over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations. The students, who have been agitating for 16 days, have announced a ‘Vidhan Sabha March’ despite the state government saying it has accepted 98 per cent of their demands.The march is scheduled to begin between 10:30 and 11 am, with students gathering at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium from 9 am, according to student leader Ravindra Paswan. He urged protesters to remain peaceful and follow constitutional norms.Speaking to ANI, Paswan said, "A march to the Vidhan Sabha and a gherao will be conducted in a peaceful and constitutional manner. Students started gathering there at 9:00 AM. The march will commence between 10:30 and 11:00 AM. I urge all students and the general public to maintain peace and adhere to constitutional norms. Since we students are leading this movement, we must demonstrate that we are disciplined and educated. Students from every district of Jharkhand are arriving for today's protest; there will be a massive turnout."A prohibitory order has been imposed within a 750-metre radius of the Jharkhand Vidhan Sabha from August 6 to 12.The restrictions will remain in force from 6 am to 10 pm each day.Police have put up barricades around the Assembly premises, with barbed wire installed at parts of the protest route to prevent demonstrators from reaching restricted areas.Ranchi SSP Rakesh Ranjan said that maintaining law and order during the march is everyone’s responsibility. "We do not want a blot on the career of any student due to disruption of law and order. Barricades have been put in place at major points with the deployment of adequate police force across the city," the SSP said.The Jharkhand Police and district administration have made elaborate security arrangements across the city ahead of the students’ ‘Vidhan Sabha March’. The government said no student would be harassed during the protest.Most schools in Ranchi will remain closed on Monday in view of the planned march, with authorities taking precautionary measures ahead of the expected turnout.The Ranchi district administration appealed to agitating students to refrain from aggressive demonstrations and cautioned against violence or illegal activities during the march to the Assembly.BJP leader Amar Bauri alleged that the party’s state unit president Aditya Sahu had been “put under house arrest” ahead of Monday’s protest.A prohibitory order was imposed in Jamshedpur from Sunday midnight in view of the protest march in Ranchi, according to an official statement.Protesters alleged that hundreds of students travelling to Ranchi from different parts of Jharkhand were being stopped by police forcefully.Student leader Ravindra Paswan urged protesters to remain peaceful and follow constitutional norms during the march, which is scheduled to begin between 10:30 and 11 am.Ranchi City SP Paras Rana addressed concerns over a viral video that appeared to show a pellet gun, clarifying that the weapon was actually a paintball gun. "If a pellet gun is being carried, it is strictly for emergency situations. Regarding the viral video--what is being mistaken for a pellet gun is actually a paintball gun; it fires soft, colored balls used to mark and identify troublemakers. It is not a pellet gun," he was quoted by ANI as saying.
Article Summary: Jharkhand police impose prohibitory orders around the assembly and strengthened security across the city as students marched against alleged recruitment exam irregularities. March is scheduled to begin between 10:30 and 11 am, with students gathering at jaipal singh munda stadium from 9 am.

NEW DELHI: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has launched a probe into irregularities in several recruitment exams in Jharkhand, including the JSSC-CGL exam, as news agency PTI quoted officials saying on Monday.The agency has taken note of an FIR filed by the state police CID and other complaints and will investigate the matter under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA).The development comes as students have been protesting for 16 days, demanding a CBI probe into alleged irregularities in recruitment exams, particularly the JSSC-CGL (Jharkhand General Graduate Level Combined Competitive Examination).The protests in Jharkhand has entered its 17th day on Monday.The students have refused to end their protest. Article Title: Bureaucratic reshuffle: Deepti Gaur Mukerjee named new higher education secretary
Article Text:
Mukerjee will now succeed Vineet Joshi, who was last month appointed as secretary, Panchayati Raj (File photo)

NEW DELHI: In a late-night bureaucratic reshuffle Monday, govt appointed Deepti Gaur Mukerjee, a 1993-batch IAS from the Madhya Pradesh cadre as new higher education secretary. This comes barely three weeks after Naresh Pal Gangwar, a Rajasthan cadre IAS officer, was named to become higher education secretary, but it was put in abeyance.His appointment had drawn public criticism on social media because his family members previously received over Rs 1 crore in govt horticulture subsidies for commercial cucumber cultivation under a National Horticulture Board scheme. The last tranche of the subsidy was released after he took charge as secretary, department of animal husbandry and dairying.As per a personnel department order, Mukerjee will now succeed Vineet Joshi, who was last month appointed as secretary, Panchayati Raj. Mukerjee is currently serving as corporate affairs secretary. Current youth affairs secretary Pallavi Jain Govil will be the new corporate affairs secretary.Sushil Kumar Lohani, officer on special duty, Cabinet Secretariat, has been appointed as chairman, Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI). Sunil Paliwal, incumbent IWAI chairman will be new youth affairs and sports secretary.Govt also appointed Assam-Meghalaya cadre IAS, Archana Verma as the new secretary of water resources and Ganga rejuvenation department by replacing incumbent secretary V L Kantha Rao.
Article Summary: Mukerjee will now succeed vineet joshi, who was last month appointed as secretary, panchayati raj. This comes barely three weeks after naresh pal gangwar, a rajasthan cadre ias officer, was named to become higher education secretary, but it was put in abeyance.

Article Title: Monsoon Session: Govt offers Amit Shah statement in Parliament, opposition doesn't relent
Article Text:
The Monsoon Session of Parliament has been marred by opposition protests since it began on July 20.

Ready to discuss every issue inside the House, says Nadda

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Govt Monday agreed to a debate in Parliament on the recent student protest and home minister Amit Shah’s statement on the issue, but it failed to break the impasse as Congress insisted that all its demands, including PM Modi’s apology for alleged police excesses against protesters and a statement on embezzlement of Ram temple funds, be met.“Congress and Rahul Gandhi have been demanding a statement from Shah from day one (of Parliament’s monsoon session). Govt is ready to hold a discussion and give a detailed response. I request Congress not to walk out during his (Shah’s) statement. It should not be scared and run away,” parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju said.The opposition, however, persisted with its protests, leading Rijiju to accuse Rahul of shifting goalposts. The leader of the opposition said all the issues raised by Congress are “non-negotiable” ."It appears that his intention is to prevent the House from functioning. Rahul Gandhi, do not run away from discussion. We are prepared to discuss every issue inside the House,” Leader of the House in Rajya Sabha J P Nadda said after Rahul was joined by Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge in rejecting govt’s proposal.Nadda also denied that police had fired at protesters on July 20.Marred by opposition protests since the session began on July 20, except for an animated debate on the NEET paper leak and related issues, LS again faced a couple of adjournments Monday before Rijiju conveyed govt’s proposal.Rijiju had put forth govt’s stand earlier at a meeting of floor leaders of different parties chaired by Speaker Om Birla, and some opposition MPs saw in it a bid to divide their ranks, as the minister made no commitment to the demand of a discussion on the theft of donations at Ram temple, a demand primarily taken by Samajwadi Party.The opposition has, however, so far not laid out the sequence in which they wanted the issues to be discussed. SP chief Akhilesh Yadav said the breach of faith of crores of devotees was not a normal issue and it must be discussed.Speaking to reporters later, both Kharge and Rahul said Shah must make a statement in Parliament on who authorised the “brutality” on students. Rahul said the country was not interested in Shah’s “fantasy conversations” on general issues but wanted to know specifically if he ordered the shooting of pellet guns and use of nail-studded lathis on students.“Shah should come clean… We are seeking his resignation,” he said.All three demands are non-negotiable, Kharge stressed, suggesting the stand-off is unlikely to end in days to come as monsoon session ends Aug 13.In a counter presser, Nadda accused Rahul of misleading people by making a baseless allegation that shots were fired at student protesters during their march to Parliament on July 20. “Rahul has been disrupting the House for over 15 days by speaking lies and spreading confusion. His intention is not to engage in discussion but to stoke anarchy,” the health minister claimed.Shah is willing to reply to every claim if Congress allows the House to function, he said, adding that the party has a history of running away from debates, recalling that it had sought a discussion on SIR but walked out during govt’s reply.
Article Summary: The monsoon session of parliament has been marred by opposition protests since it began on july 20. Congress insisted that all its demands, including pm modi’s apology for alleged police excesses against protesters, be met. The leader of the opposition said all the issues raised by congress are “non-negotiable’

Article Title: Safari in snow leopard home? Conservationists say Ladakh is no Kaziranga
Article Text:
Ladakh has planned to introduce guided wildlife safaris on popular snow leopard and bird-watching trails.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

SRINAGAR: A safari car can roll past a rhino in Kaziranga. In Ranthambore, it can track a tiger. Put that car in Ladakh. For its elusive snow leopards — masters of camouflage in a landscape where survival depends on staying unseen — the question is whether tourism can get close enough to see them without making them disappear for good.Ladakh has planned to introduce guided wildlife safaris on popular snow leopard and bird-watching trails, triggering warnings from conservationists that turning a fragile high-altitude wilderness into a tourist circuit could disturb wildlife, commercialise off-roading and open the door to roads, eateries and other tourism infrastructure.“You cannot see a snow leopard from a jeep unless you do something illegal like placing bait or a sheep to lure it,” said Dr MK Ranjitsinh, emeritus member of Wildlife Trust of India, who has spent nearly 50 years shaping conservation strategies and played a key role in framing the Wildlife (Protection) Act of 1972 and Project Tiger.“Kaziranga is not Ladakh and Ranthambore is not Ladakh. The ecology is completely different,” he added.In Ladakh’s open valleys, vehicles can be visible from miles away. Vegetation is concentrated along valley bottoms, drawing animals there to feed and drink. “Are you taking a safari there?” he asked.Ladakh is home to 477 of India’s estimated 718 snow leopards — the country’s largest population. It also supports more than 38 mammal species, 340 bird species and 1,800 vascular plant species.But spotting a snow leopard is a needle-in-a-haystack affair. Its thick, mottled coat melts into rocky slopes, while steep, remote terrain gives it a vast natural advantage.The Ladakh govt spokesperson said lieutenant governor Vinai Kumar Saxena has directed the forest department to introduce guided safaris modelled on national parks such as Kaziranga and Ranthambore, using specially designed open-back vehicles operated by trained local drivers and guides. According to govt, the move is aimed at preventing illegal off-roading and disturbance of wildlife.The plan was cleared at the first governing body meeting of Snow Leopard and High-Altitude Nature Conservation Society, chaired by Saxena. Forest officials have been asked to explore routes across Hemis national park, Changthang and Karakoram wildlife sanctuaries, besides Nubra, Zanskar, Sham, Kargil and Drass.Ranjitsinh fears a different road ahead. “Wildlife safari may be good in principle but in practice it could be a disaster,” he said, warning that tourism and hotel lobbies could eventually overwhelm govt controls. “There will be demands for more roads, eating places and other infrastructure. Eventually, the whole landscape could turn into a festival.”A wildlife official said safaris work best where animals occur in large concentrations or herds — unlike Himalayan and Trans-Himalayan terrain. Ladakh already has roads across its protected areas, with tourist vehicles accessing most zones except some restricted border regions.“What they actually plan is to regularise and commercialise off-roading,” the official said, warning that vehicles could be allowed into fragile meadows for a price.Kaziranga and Ranthambore were built into India’s safari imagination. Ladakh’s proposed safari would venture into an entirely different world. Its snow leopards are scattered across an unforgiving landscape where the first rule of spotting one is knowing where not to look.
Article Summary: Ladakh has planned to introduce guided wildlife safaris on popular snow leopard and bird-watching trails. Conservationists warn that turning a fragile high-altitude wilderness into a tourist circuit could disturb wildlife, commercialise off-roading and open the door to roads.

Article Title: Amid delimitation Bill buzz, NCP-SP MPs meet PM Modi
Article Text:

(With inputs from Anurag Bende in Pune)

NEW DELHI: Eight Lok Sabha MPs of NCP(SP) led by Supriya Sule met PM Narendra Modi on Monday amid buzz that govt is eyeing their support for its constitution amendment bill for delimitation and indications from the governing alliance that it has two-thirds support in Parliament required for the legislation’s passage.Sule and her colleagues said their meeting with Modi was focused on development issues concerning Maharashtra, but, coming as it did days after the party’s patriarch Sharad Pawar met PM ostensibly over similar matters, political circles were agog with speculation that the regional party was coming closer to BJP over its centrepiece bill.Last month, Sule had said her party may consider backing delimitation if all states see an equal 50% rise in their Lok Sabha seats — something which, interestingly, forms the core of the bill — while insisting that NCP(SP) will take a final decision in consultation with its opposition allies.Meanwhile, Congress is upset over its ally NCP(SP)’S talks with the top brass of BJP at the Centre and in the state.“When the opposition has cornered Prime Minister Modi and home minister Shah over recent police violence during CJP [Cockroach Janta Party] protest at Jantar Mantar, such meetings of opposition members give the wrong message. Ultimately, the leadership of that party will have to decide which path to follow,” a senior Congress member said.Stressing that there was no discussion about the delimitation bill during the meeting, Shirur NCP (SP) MP Amol Kolhe said, “The purpose of the meeting was to seek intervention of the Prime Minister in some of the key issues such as agrarian crisis in the state, long pending Pune-Nashik railway project and infrastructure problems faced by industries.”Former CM and senior Congress functionary Prithviraj Chavan said, “I do not know the agenda of such meetings, but apart from such scheduled meetings, some secret meetings also keep happening. Some members of the parties in the govt have told me that they will be attempting to split NCP (SP). I do not know if the meeting had anything to do with it.”NCP (SP) chief Sharad Pawar met Modi last month. A meeting between Supriya and Shah followed.As these meetings were happening in Delhi, the party’s former state president Jayant Patil held closed-door talks with CM Devendra Fadnavis in the latter’s Mumbai residence. NCP seniors Praful Patel and Sunil Tatkare were also present there.
Article Summary: Eight lok sabha mps of ncp(sp) led by supriya sule met pm narendra modi on monday. Meeting comes amid buzz that govt is eyeing their support for its constitution amendment bill for delimitation. Congress is upset over its ally ncp (sp)’s talks with the top brass of bjp at the centre and in the state.

Article Title: 'Don't fall into political trap': Jharkhand CM Soren writes open letter to protesting students
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Jharkhand chief minister Hemant Soren on Monday thanked the officials and security agencies for "handling" the student protest march against the alleged irregularities in the state recruitment examinations with "restraint, sensitivity and complete responsibility. "Soren posted an open letter addressing the students on X and said that the government has listened to their concerns and assured them that their demands will be addressed with seriousness and sensitivity."You have raised your voice for your demands in a peaceful manner. In a democracy, it is your right to express your views, and it is the government's responsibility to respect your voice. The government has heard you. Our senior ministers have been in constant dialogue with you, and I assure you that action will be taken on your demands with utmost seriousness and sensitivity," he said.Further, Soren said that the government's objective is to eliminate shortcomings in the examination system."In the past few days, you have seen that the government has spared no one, no matter who the guilty party is. Our clear objective is to eliminate such shortcomings in the system so that no student has to face trouble in the future.We want to make the examination system more transparent, technology-enabled, secure and accountable. Your participation in this change is the most important," he said.In his post, Soren also appealed to the students not to fall into the trap of a political narrative."Our effort is that Jharkhand should not just discuss problems, but set a new example of solutions from here. I also understand that amid your peaceful movement, some people from the opposition have tried to spoil the atmosphere and mislead students for political gain. I appeal to all of you not to fall into the trap of any such political narrative," the chief minister said."You are the future of Jharkhand. It is not about ignoring your voice, but listening to it and resolving your problems - that is our responsibility. I will reiterate my point: let us resolve this issue together through dialogue and trust," he added.This comes after thousands of students participated in the 'Vidhan Sabha Gherao' march organised by the JPSC-JSSC Reform Morcha against alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations.During the march, several agitators and four policemen were injured in a clash near the Jharkhand assembly, as police used water cannons, tear gas and lathi-charged job aspirants protesting against alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations, officials said.Earlier on Sunday, Jharkhand students protesting irregularities in recruitment exams rejected the Hemant Soren-led government's claim that 98% of their demands had been accepted. They said only three of the 13 exams they wanted cancelled had been scrapped.The students accused the JMM-led government of "spreading lies" and said they would continue their peaceful protest.At a press conference, a student leader said, "The Jharkhand government is spreading lies that it fulfilled 98% of our demands. It cancelled only three of the 13 exams sought by us."The protesters are demanding a CBI probe into alleged irregularities in all recruitment exams conducted by the state. Student leader Ravindra Paswan accused the government of insisting on a CID probe, which he claimed was known for "cover-ups".
Article Summary: Jharkhand chief minister hemant soren thanked officials and security agencies for "handling" the student protest march with "restraint, sensitivity and complete responsibility" soren posted an open letter addressing the students on x and said that the government has listened to their concerns.

Article Title: Ram Rahim’s acquittal in journalist murder case needs consideration: Supreme Court
Article Text:
Rahim’s counsel said HC had recorded a categorical finding that the key witness could not be believed

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHIi: Supreme Court on Monday admitted a petition challenging acquittal of Dera Sacha Sauda chief Gurmeet Ram Rahim , who is serving a 20-year sentence for sexually assaulting two female disciples, in the 2002 murder of Sirsa-based journalist Ram Chander Chhatrapati.A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana overruled protests by Rahim’s counsel R Basant that it was a case of acquittal and that the state had not filed any appeal against the acquittal.“This matter requires consideration. It is a reversal of conviction (recorded by the trial court). It is not an acquittal affirmed by HC. We are equally conscious that the state (CBI) will not appeal against the acquittal,” it said. The trial court had convicted Rahim and sentenced him to life imprisonment in Jan 2019.Admitting a petition by Arindam Chhatrapati, the complainant and son of the murdered journalist, the bench requisitioned the trial court records, including witness statements, for scrutiny. It posted final hearing of the matter in Nov last week.Basant said HC had recorded a categorical finding that the key witness could not be believed at all.“We will examine the special circumstances attending to the examination of the key witness and whether the appreciation of his evidence is appropriate,” responded the bench.The appellant said, “Despite affirming the categorical findings of the trial court on the existence of a conspiracy for the commission of Chhatrapati’s murder and upholding the convictions of the three co-accused under Section 120-B IPC read with Section 302 IPC, HC incorrectly arrived at a conclusion that participation of Baba Gurmeet Singh in the conspiracy is not proved.”Finding lapses in the local police probe, Punjab and Haryana HC had in Nov 2003, almost a year after the murder, transferred the investigations to the CBI. The key witness, referred to by the SC, is the ex-driver of Rahim.
Article Summary: Supreme court on monday admitted a petition challenging acquittal of dera sacha sauda chief gurmeet ram rahim. Rahim is serving a 20-year sentence for sexually assaulting two female disciples, in the 2002 murder of sirsa-based journalist ram chander chhatrapati.

Article Title: Government says LoP Rahul Gandhi to sit per the table of precedence during Independence Day
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Defence secretary RK Singh on Monday said leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi has been invited to the Independence Day celebrations at the Red Fort on August 15 and will be seated immediately after the Union Cabinet ministers."Leader of opposition has been invited, and his seating would be as per the Table of Precedence, which is exactly after Cabinet ministers," Singh told news agency ANI.In 2024, Rahul Gandhi's seating arrangement during the Independence Day celebrations had triggered a row after the Congress criticised the government for giving him a seat in the "fifth row" and calling the move a display of "pettiness" and a disregard for democratic norms. Officials from the ministry of defence, which organises the event, clarified that the 5th row seating arrangement for LoP was necessiated because of adjustment of 4 Olympic medalist in each row along with the ministers after first two rows.Earlier this year, the Congress had again accused the Centre of violating established protocol and undermining democratic decorum after Rahul Gandhi and Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge were seated in the third row during the Republic Day celebrations.However, the defence ministry refuted the charge and stated that the seating arrangements were done as per the "Table of Precedence".According to the Warrant of Precedence issued by the President's secretariat, seating arrangements at state and ceremonial occasions are decided based on constitutional rank and office, and not political affiliation. The Table of Precedence is a protocol list that applies to state and ceremonial occasions, including national events such as Republic Day celebrations, and has no application to the day-to-day functioning of the government.As per this, the leader of opposition in Lok Sabha has a rank equivalent to that of a Cabinet minister.
Article Summary: Defence secretary rk singh on monday said leader of opposition in lok sabha rahul gandhi has been invited to the independence day celebrations at the red fort on august 15. He said gandhi will be seated immediately after the union cabinet ministers.

Article Title: CM defends FCRA amendments, rejects ‘anti-Christian’ charge
Article Text:

Nagpur: Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis on Monday defended proposed amendments to Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act (FCRA), alleging that a section of organizations receiving foreign funds had used the money for "anti-national activities" and that the changes were intended to curb such misuse rather than target any particular community.Responding to criticism from Congress, which has described the proposed amendments as "anti-Christian", he said FCRA framework applies uniformly to every organisation receiving foreign contributions, irrespective of religion or community."The reason for bringing the FCRA amendments is that some organisations have been bringing foreign money into the country and using it for anti-national activities. That has to stop," Fadnavis said."Those who are doing good work have nothing to worry about. There will be an FCRA mechanism and their licences will be protected," he said.Rejecting the allegation that the amendments specifically target Christian organizations, Fadnavis said the law governs all entities receiving foreign donations."This is not a question of one community. It is applicable to every organization that receives foreign donations, irrespective of its community," he said.Fadnavis said anyone with reservations about the proposed legislation should raise them during the parliamentary process, adding that Union govt was open to hearing different views."I believe that if anyone has objections, they should raise them in Parliament. The govt of India is receptive," he said.Referring to statements made in the United States on the proposed amendments, Fadnavis questioned why individuals outside India were reacting to the legislation."Some people in the US have commented on the FCRA Amendment Bill. What does that mean? The very purpose of these amendments becomes clear from such reactions," he said, without elaborating further.The CM reiterated that the objective of the proposed amendments was to ensure accountability in the use of foreign contributions and prevent their misuse, while protecting organizations carrying out lawful activities.
Article Summary: Devendra fadnavis defends proposed amendments to foreign contribution (regulation) act. He says fcra framework applies uniformly to every organisation receiving foreign contributions, irrespective of religion or community. "those who are doing good work have nothing to worry about," he says.

Article Title: J&K police foil government staffer bid to trap ex-lover’s husband in drug case
Article Text:

SRINAGAR: J&K police on Monday claimed to have busted a plot by a 51-year-old govt employee to get his former lover’s newlywed husband arrested in a narcotics case. The accused allegedly couriered illegal drugs to the husband in an attempt to resume his affair with the 27-year-old woman.Police have arrested the accused, Tariq Ahmad Sofi, employed with wildlife department in Ganderbal.The case came to light after police in Ganderbal district received information about a suspected drug consignment being sent through a courier service. Police intercepted the parcel shipped from Uttar Pradesh’s Kanpur and deployed a sniffer dog to examine it.“It contained around 4 kg of a powder-like substance which, on FSL examination, tested positive for cocaine, having huge value in the international market,” police said.Four packets, each containing 80 grams of what police described as “pure charas”, and strips of suspected psychotropic tablets were seized.The consignment was addressed to the woman’s husband, a poultry farm owner, who told police he was expecting poultry feed from a person who had contacted him through WhatsApp. He denied any knowledge of the drugs.Police then examined the husband’s background, as well as the phone records of the newlyweds, who married just a month ago.Investigators said the woman’s phone records provided the first major clue, leading them to Sofi, who had arranged the consignment through a friend identified as Areeb.Police are investigating whether the woman was part of the plot.Investigators are also scanning Areeb’s movements and possible links to Saudi Arabia after his phone records showed he called the poultry farm owner from that country. Police are also trying to establish how the drugs were procured and dispatched to Ganderbal through the courier.“We are also investigating whether the drugs were originally procured in the Valley and then dispatched to Kanpur, just to be couriered back to the poultry farm owner,” police said.
Article Summary: Police have arrested the accused, tariq ahmad sofi, employed with wildlife department in ganderbal. The accused allegedly couriered illegal drugs to the husband in an attempt to resume his affair with the 27-year-old woman.
